clue.text: Capital needed by a big place — as much as can be produced

definitions.text: as much as can be produced

parts.note: a capital letter is informally a cap, as in 'write it in caps'
taken as written
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A capital city needs funds, and a big place is told to produce all it can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts as money or a chief city, but here it is the short word for a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity is the maximum output a factory or system is able to deliver.

clue.text: Egyptian policeman on the beat in conversation

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a cop is a police officer

indicators.note: in conversation means the word is spoken, so its sound is used

parts.note: a tick is a beat of a clock

explanation.surface: An Egyptian officer patrols his beat, chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'policeman on the beat' reads as a patrol; it splits as COP placed on TIC, which sounds like tick.
explanation.definitionFit: Coptic is the language and church of Egypt's Christians, descended from ancient Egyptian.

clue.text: Fruit has to simmer on quietly when cooked

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: cooked means altered or rearranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Fruit must keep simmering gently during cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooked' rearranges SIMMER ON into ERSIMMON, which follows P.
explanation.definitionFit: The persimmon is an orange tomato-like fruit, also called the sharon fruit.

clue.text: Concern for some of the foot-soldiers

definitions.meaning: a concern is a business or firm
an army unit of infantry, smaller than a battalion

explanation.surface: Worry on behalf of some infantrymen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' reads as worry but means a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is both a commercial firm and an infantry subunit of around a hundred soldiers.

clue.text: Money raising, for example, causes suspicion

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Fundraising, for instance, arouses suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns EG into GE. 'suspicion' means a faint trace, as in a suspicion of garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight hint or trace, as is a suspicion of something.

clue.text: Occult lore about a lake in Wales

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about
Bala Lake (Llyn Tegid) is the largest natural lake in Wales

explanation.surface: Somebody spreads mystical teachings about a Welsh lake.
explanation.walkthrough: BALA is a lake and town in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabala is the Jewish mystical tradition, so more widely any secret esoteric doctrine.

clue.text: A northern town free from ground rent

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: free from says the word for ground is taken out

parts.note: Sunderland is a city in north-east England
land is ground

explanation.surface: A northern town escapes ground rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground rent' looks like a single property term; 'rent' alone is the definition, meaning torn apart. Sunderland is in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something torn apart is split into pieces, as in a veil rent in two.

clue.text: Solitary corporal on easy sector

indicators.note: sector says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lone corporal has an easy patch to look after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sector' is a section of the phrase, picking out the letters spanning corporal, on and easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary means being by oneself, with no company.

clue.text: A declaration of independence by Conservative member of the hearing

parts.note: taken as written
UDI was Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence of 1965
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory MP declares independence at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: UDI is the famous 1965 Rhodesian declaration; Tory is the nickname of a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditory means relating to the sense of hearing.

clue.text: Inveigh against dunderhead — he's holding one up

indicators.note: holding says one word is held inside another

parts.note: a dunce is a stupid person

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody rails against an idiot holding up a single finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ONE into ENO, which DUNCE holds after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, as to inveigh against is to protest bitterly.

clue.text: Consultation on a big case brings to light a double meaning

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another is written after it

parts.note: a portmanteau is a large travelling bag that opens into two halves
to have a word with someone is to hold a brief consultation

explanation.surface: Discussions about a major legal case uncover an ambiguity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big case' sounds legal; it is luggage. The blended word (like brunch) packs two meanings into one, as Lewis Carroll explained.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a blend, like smog from smoke and fog, carries the senses of two words at once.

clue.text: One thing in China to copy

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: in says the word for thing goes inside the word for China

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a friend
it is a pronoun standing for a thing

explanation.surface: Someone copies a single Chinese object.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so China (capitalised to mislead) is MATE; IT goes in after its M.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or reproduce someone or something.

clue.text: Something left over — spare pieces with shirt tail

parts.note: an odd sock or glove is a spare one with no partner
chessmen and draughtsmen are pieces, so men

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, here the end of shirt

explanation.surface: A scrap of leftover cloth includes spare bits and the tail of a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a remnant or stray leftover item.

clue.text: When in trouble, Englishmen pray to heaven

indicators.note: being in trouble suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: English is abbreviated E, and men stays as written

explanation.surface: In a crisis, English people turn to prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' scrambles E and MEN (from Englishmen) with PRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The empyrean is the highest heaven, the realm of pure fire or light in old cosmology.

clue.text: Optical aid you can't see through if it's back to front

indicators.note: back to front says the front part moves to the back

parts.note: an artificial eye made of glass gives no sight

explanation.surface: A lens that is opaque when held the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: A glass eye is an artificial eye; 'back to front' moves GLASS from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass is a single lens or monocle worn to help sight.

clue.text: Lineage right for a fast horse

parts.note: a race is a line of descent or ancestry

explanation.surface: A bloodline proves suitable for a speedy horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is any animal or vehicle built for speed, such as a racehorse.

clue.text: Sort of ship in a bottle, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a vessel carrying cargo in standard steel boxes
a bottle is one example of a receptacle

explanation.surface: A model ship built inside a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints the hobby of a ship in a bottle; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A container ship carries freight boxes, and any vessel that holds things, like a bottle, is a receptacle of that name.

clue.text: Cook's vessel can pause in this resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it means sort the letters again

explanation.surface: A chef's pot can rest at this holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place; read as re-sort it rearranges CAN PAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucepan is a cooking pot with a long handle.

clue.text: Inane fashion for a female hillbilly

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Silly clothes styles for a backwoods woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun about clothes; as a verb it reworks INANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is a girl's name, standing for a country girl like the sharpshooting Annie of Annie Get Your Gun.

clue.text: Pride in rise of best-seller

indicators.note: in a down clue the rise of a word makes it read upwards

parts.note: a best-selling book is a number one tale: NO for number, I for one, then TALE

explanation.surface: Someone feels proud as a best-selling book climbs the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' turns NO I TALE (a top-selling story) upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is joyful exhilaration, close to the glowing satisfaction of pride.

clue.text: Still air for vespers

parts.note: still as in 'still more' means even
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A calm tune for an evening church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' and 'air' suggest calm weather; they are EVEN (as in even better) and a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening prayer office, the Anglican form of which is sung as an evening service.

clue.text: Waste food that's bad for sheep

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: something harmful to sheep

parts.note: scrap is leftover food, as in scraps for the dog
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Leftover food that is harmful for sheep to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'food' seems a separate piece; 'Waste food' together is SCRAP, and 'that's' is IE (that is).
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal brain disease of sheep and goats.

clue.text: She is burning electricity

parts.note: a fire that is in is still alight
the grid is the network supplying electricity

explanation.surface: A woman is wasting power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning electricity' suggests waste; IN means alight and GRID is the power network. 'She' is the definition: a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a woman's given name, as with the actress Bergman.

clue.text: College term for a whistle of disapproval

parts.note: Cat's is the informal name of St Catharine's College, Cambridge
to term something is to call it by a name

explanation.surface: A university term earns a whistle of disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like a period of study; as a verb it means call. St Catharine's is a Cambridge college, known as Cat's.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a shrill whistle or jeering cry from an audience showing displeasure.

clue.text: Sort of water to use for a shot in the arm?

definitions.meaning: a carbonated mixer flavoured with quinine

explanation.surface: Which drink to use as an injection?
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a fizzy quinine mixer, and a tonic is anything that restores vigour.

clue.text: Profit on public house contract

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another is written after it

parts.note: a bar is the drinking room of a pub
profit is gain

explanation.surface: Earnings from a pub agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: A public house is a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is a deal or agreement between parties.

clue.text: Lines eggs up — well done!

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the national railway lines

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: Someone sets out eggs in rows and is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail; 'up' turns OVA into AVO.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is a cry of approval meaning excellent.

clue.text: The writer makes his point here

definitions.text: The writer makes his point here

parts.words: The writer makes his point here
parts.note: the writer is a pencil rather than an author, and its point is the sharpened tip it gets in this gadget

explanation.surface: An author arrives at the crux of the argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The device sharpens a pencil, which is the writer, giving it a point.

clue.text: The creed for nine out of a hundred English

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of nine are put out of order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Only nine people in a hundred English share a certain belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles NINE with C to give NICEN, and E for English follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nicene Creed, from the Council of Nicaea, is the statement of faith recited in Christian liturgy.

clue.text: Turned down, as boxers are bound to be

definitions.meaning: pages turned down at the corner, as a bookmark

definitions.text: as boxers are bound to be
definitions.meaning: boxer dogs have ears, so they are eared like a dog

explanation.surface: Something folded over, as fighters inevitably are.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers are dogs, not fighters, and 'bound' hints at the binding of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-eared pages have folded-down corners, like a hound's floppy ears; a dog literally has dog's ears.
